questions.stem: Why does the temperature remain constant during a change of state, even though energy is being supplied?

options.text: The energy is used to overcome forces between particles rather than increasing kinetic energy
The particles stop moving during a change of state
The thermometer stops working at the melting point
The energy is being lost to the surroundings

questions.explanation: During a change of state, the energy being supplied is used to overcome the forces between particles (breaking intermolecular bonds), not to increase the kinetic energy of the particles. Since temperature is a measure of kinetic energy, the temperature stays constant until the state change is complete. This energy is called latent heat.
